subsystems.name: Neural recorder
subsystems.role: captures the sender's brain activity with enough resolution to infer intended messages.

subsystems.name: Neural decoder
subsystems.role: translates recorded activity into a transmission code.

subsystems.name: Transmission link
subsystems.role: sends the code from sender to receiver.

subsystems.name: Neural encoder
subsystems.role: converts the code into stimulation parameters for the receiver.

subsystems.name: Neural stimulator
subsystems.role: delivers patterned stimulation to the receiver's sensory cortex.

subsystems.name: Calibration system
subsystems.role: aligns the two brains' representations through training and feedback.

buildSteps.title: Capture high-resolution neural activity
buildSteps.detail: Use implanted microelectrodes or non-invasive sensors to record the sender's brain signals with sufficient spatial and temporal detail.

buildSteps.title: Decode intended messages
buildSteps.detail: Train machine-learning models to recognise patterns that correspond to specific thoughts, words or commands.

buildSteps.title: Define a shared code
buildSteps.detail: Create a mapping between neural patterns and a symbolic code or direct stimulation patterns that both brains can interpret.

buildSteps.title: Develop precise neural stimulation
buildSteps.detail: Build hardware that can safely and selectively activate targeted regions of the receiver's sensory cortex without damage.

buildSteps.title: Close the loop in real time
buildSteps.detail: Integrate recording, decoding, transmission and stimulation into a low-latency pipeline that operates in under a second.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate across brains
buildSteps.detail: Use feedback so sender and receiver adapt to each other's neural signatures, refining the translation over repeated sessions.

buildSteps.title: Validate in trials and scale
buildSteps.detail: Start with simple commands in animals, move to limited human trials under medical oversight, then improve bandwidth, safety and reliability.

prerequisites.why: invasive arrays can record hundreds of neurons, but non-invasive methods capture far less information.
we can decode motor intent and some speech, but not arbitrary concepts or abstract thoughts.
TMS can activate regions non-invasively; implanted microstimulation works in animals but is invasive and limited in resolution.
how the brain represents meaning across individuals is not fully known, making a universal code difficult.
medical device rules exist, but brain-to-brain communication raises new questions of consent, privacy and identity.

pathway.milestone: laboratory demonstrations of simple brain-to-brain communication in animals and basic human tasks
pathway.unlocks: proof that direct neural transmission is possible.

pathway.milestone: non-invasive systems for basic communication in medical settings, such as helping locked-in patients
pathway.unlocks: assistive communication without speech or movement.

pathway.milestone: invasive high-bandwidth systems for richer, faster transfer of complex ideas
pathway.unlocks: direct sharing of detailed thoughts between individuals.

pathway.milestone: consumer or general use, if safety and ethics are resolved
pathway.unlocks: new forms of human interaction and collaboration.
